Weather Update: 15 नवंबर के बाद बदलेगा उत्तर भारत का मौसम, कानपुर में सुबह धुंध दोपहर में धूप

HighLights
कानपुर में सुबह धुंध, दिन में तेज धूप और रात में ठंडक।
अधिकतम तापमान 31.5, न्यूनतम 14.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया।
15 नवंबर के बाद उत्तर भारत में मौसमी बदलाव, बूंदाबांदी संभव।
जागरण संवाददाता, कानपुर। दीपावली के बाद बढ़े प्रदूषण के बीच मौसम का मिजाज भी बदलने लगा है। शुक्रवार सुबह शहर में धुंध छाई रही, जबकि दिन चढ़ने के साथ आसमान साफ हुआ और तेज धूप निकली। दोपहर में गर्मी का एहसास हुआ तो सुबह और रात में हल्की ठंडक बनी रही। अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से तीन डिग्री अधिक 31.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 14.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जो सामान्य से 2.1 डिग्री अधिक रहा।
मौसम विशेषज्ञ डा. एसएन सुनील पांडेय ने बताया कि फिलहाल वर्षा की संभावना नहीं है। अगले 24 घंटे मौसम साफ और शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है। उत्तर-पश्चिमी हवा के कारण रात के तापमान में गिरावट सीमित है, जबकि दिन में तेज धूप तापमान बढ़ा रही है। इसी वजह से सुबह-रात हल्की ठंड और दोपहर में गर्मी का एहसास हो रहा है।
उन्होंने बताया कि देश में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ, चक्रवाती परिसंचरण, निम्न दबाव क्षेत्र और ट्रफ लाइन जैसी मौसमी प्रणालियां सक्रिय हो रही हैं। इनके प्रभाव से अरब सागर समेत अन्य क्षेत्रों से नमी वाली हवाएं उत्तर भारत की ओर आ सकती हैं। इससे पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में बर्फबारी और पंजाब, हरियाणा तथा पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के कुछ हिस्सों में बादलों की आवाजाही हो सकती है। कहीं-कहीं हल्की बूंदाबांदी के आसार भी बन सकते हैं। इन मौसमी बदलावों का असर 15 नवंबर के बाद देखने को मिल सकता है।
इधर, चिड़ियाघर में सर्दियों का मेन्यू तैयार
सर्दियों की दस्तक के साथ ही कानपुर चिड़ियाघर में वन्यजीवों की खुराक बदल दी गई हैं। ठंड में पर्याप्त ऊर्जा देने के लिए चिड़ियाघर प्रशासन ने वन्यजीवों की खुराक बढ़ाने के साथ ही उसमें पौष्टिक आहार भी शामिल किया है। अब पक्षियों को रोजाना उबला अंडा, मूंगफली और अखरोट परोसे जा रहे हैं तो भालुओं की खुराक में शहद दिया जाने लगा है। दूसरी ओर शेर और बाघ के भोजन में मीट की मात्रा बढ़ाकर नौ किलो तक कर दी गई है। शाकाहारी वन्यजीवों को गुड़ और चना खिलाया जा रहा है।

Developers at a site earmarked for the construction of the UK's largest tissue paper mill say they are "disappointed" after the Finnish toilet roll manufacturer behind the proposal pulled out.
Planning permission for the Metsä development on a 211-acre site in Goole was granted in September 2025.
At the time, Metsä said the facility, which would cover about three million sq ft (279,000 sq m) and support up to 400 direct jobs.
Wykeland Group, which holds the long-term development rights for the site, said it was now speaking to other companies. Metsä has been approached for comment.
Dominic Gibbons, managing director of Wykeland Group, said: "We're disappointed that Metsä Tissue has decided not to proceed with this development following the substantial amount of work, over the past three years, by ourselves and other stakeholders.
"However, the site now has full planning consent for three million sq ft of manufacturing and high-bay warehousing space, and benefits from attractive Freeport financial incentives, so it offers a very appealing investment proposition.
"We had put plans in motion in anticipation of Metsä's decision and we're now talking to prospective alternative end users who are interested in realising the potential of this key site."
Metsä previously said the mill, which would be capable of producing 240,000 tonnes of fresh fibre-based tissue paper per year, would increase self-sufficiency for tissue in the UK from about 40% to around 85%.
Goole is one of three Humber Freeport tax sites, along with Hull East and Able Humber Port, near Immingham.
Freeports, external are special areas within the UK where different economic regulations apply along with tax and customs incentives.

Assam CM mourns loss of life in Kaziranga accident; directs immediate relief measures
Guwahati (Assam) [India], November 13 (ANI): Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Friday expressed profound grief over the tragic accident in Kaziranga earlier today and conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones.
Terming the incident as deeply distressing, the Chief Minister said that the loss of life has shaken everyone and that his thoughts and prayers are with the bereaved families.
He added that while no words can lessen their pain, the Government and the people of Assam stand firmly with them in this hour of grief.
The Chief Minister, who is currently on a two-day official tour of Biswanath district, is closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Golaghat District Commissioner and Minister for Panchayat and Rural Development Atul Bora. Atul Bora was present at the accident site and personally oversaw the ongoing relief and rescue operations.
Sarma has also directed Education Minister Ranoj Pegu to proceed to the site immediately and extend all possible assistance.
The Chief Minister has directed the concerned authorities to ensure that the injured receive immediate and the best possible medical attention.
He has also called for all necessary arrangements to be made in connection with the accident.
Sarma has prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured and strength and courage for the bereaved families to bear this irreparable loss.
The Chief Minister will visit Golaghat district tomorrow to take stock of the situation.
Meanwhile, several political leaders across party lines have expressed deep shock and grief following the head-on collision in Assam's Kaziranga National Park area, which claimed over two dozen lives.
Speaking on the tragic incident, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA Taranga Gogoi described the event as profoundly distressing for the state.
Highlighting the scale of the disaster, which reports indicate resulted in 25 to 26 fatalities, he appealed directly to commercial transport operators.
'This is extremely tragic news for Assam. No one ever expects such an accident to occur. Yet, this accident has happened, and reports indicate that 25 to 26 people have lost their lives. It is a deeply distressing incident...I urge all drivers of commercial trucks and buses to be mindful of their speed. In this case, not only did the driver lose his own life, but he also took 25 others with him. We all need to act responsibly and adhere to speed limits,' Taranga Gogoi told ANI.
Echoing similar concerns over frequent mishaps, BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa extended his condolences and visited the injured undergoing treatment at Jorhat Medical College.
'This is truly terrible. Road accidents are occurring all too frequently. The government has implemented very strict regulations, including speed limits and the deployment of interceptor vehicles along the roads even in the Kaziranga area. How this specific incident occurred will only be revealed through an initial inquiry; I do not have the details yet. As soon as I learned of the accident, I rushed to Jorhat Medical College. I can see that the medical team is handling the situation well, and the families of the victims are also present,' Tasa told reporters.
The tragedy has triggered a sharp political debate over highway maintenance. Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi launched a scathing critique of the state's transport infrastructure, linking recurring highway fatalities to systemic flaws and oversight failures.
'The highways in Assam have become a den of corruption. The quality of construction is so poor that accidents are taking place every month. I don't know why the Government of India is collecting tolls, and I don't know why the Government of India is not maintaining proper highways. It is just unfortunate. This could have been totally avoided, but it is happening solely because of corruption, the greed of contractors, and their nexus with politicians, which forces ordinary people to suffer,' Gogoi told ANI.
The remarks came after multiple fatalities were feared following the head-on collision between a passenger vehicle and a truck in Assam's Golaghat district on Friday in the Rongajaan area near the Kaziranga National Park, police said.
At least 24 people were killed following a severe head-on collision between a passenger vehicle and a container truck in Assam's Golaghat district on Friday.
The tragedy occurred in the Rongajaan area near the Kaziranga National Park, police said.
State Minister and Bokakhat MLA Atul Bora, who rushed to the accident site to personally oversee rescue and relief operations, provided an update over the phone regarding the casualties and medical response.
'24 people died in the accident so far, and 11 injured persons were shifted to Jorhat Medical College & Hospital,' Bora told ANI, adding that other survivors receiving medical attention 'were admitted at Bokakhat Civil Hospital.'
The police official confirmed that several other individuals sustained injuries in the accident and have been rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.
Rescue and relief operations are currently underway at the site.Further details are awaited. (ANI)
